title: A relative dualizing complex restricts on an affine chart to the algebraic relative dualizing complex
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)

difficulty_reason: For a flat locally finite presentation morphism X -> S with relative dualizing complex (K, xi), the lemma asserts that for any commutative square with open immersions Spec(A) -> X and Spec(R) -> S, the restriction of K to Spec(A) corresponds, via Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-affine-compare-bounded, to a relative dualizing complex for R -> A in the sense of Dualizing Complexes, Definition labelled dualizing-definition-relative-dualizing-complex (statement lines 7270-7315). Since formation of RSheafHom commutes with restriction to opens, the proof may assume X = Spec(A) and S = Spec(R), and it notes that relatively perfect objects are pseudo-coherent, hence quasi-coherent, by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-pseudo-coherent, so the statement makes sense (proof lines 7317-7324). The compatibility of Delta_*, Lpr_1^* and RSheafHom with the algebraic side is then supplied by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemmas labelled perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-pushforward, perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-pullback and perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom; for the last one the proof observes that Lpr_1^*K is S-perfect hence bounded below and that Delta_*O_X is pseudo-coherent, which translates into A being pseudo-coherent as an A otimes_R A-module by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-more-relative-pseudo-coherent-is-moot applied to R -> A otimes_R A -> A (proof lines 7326-7345). This recovers exactly the conditions of the algebraic definition and the proof is complete (proof lines 7345-7348). Checking that each operation in the definition is compatible with the affine comparison, including the pseudo-coherence of the diagonal, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
